recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which power of x you divide by, and which terms are left at the end.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Divide throughout by x³
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both lines are cubic, so x³ is the divisor. Show the divided form before letting anything approach 0.
lines: As x → ∞ both lines increase without bound,
so this is the indeterminate form ∞/∞.
The highest power of x present is x³.
(dividing the top and the bottom by the same non-zero

lines.text: number does not change the fraction)

lines: Divide every term of both lines by x³ (x ≠ 0):

recall.must_convey: That both lines are divided by x³, the highest power of x.
accept: divide the top and the bottom by x cubed
x cubed is the highest power so divide by it
take x cube common from both lines
x cube tho rendu lines ni divide cheyyali
divide throughout by the highest power which is x cubed

steps.why: Direct substitution gives ∞/∞. Dividing by x³ leaves a constant plus terms of the form c/xⁿ on each line, and every such term approaches 0.
common_mistakes: Dividing by x² and leaving an x in both lines.
Dividing only the numerator by x³ and leaving the denominator as it is.
steps.memory_tip: A cube on top and a cube below: divide by the cube.

steps.label: Let each 1/x term approach 0
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Box 11/13. It does not reduce — 11 and 13 are both prime, so the fraction is already in lowest terms.

lines.text: (a fixed number divided by a growing power of x goes to 0)

recall.must_convey: That the remaining terms approach 0, leaving the ratio 11/13.
accept: everything with x in the denominator goes to zero leaving eleven over thirteen
the answer is eleven by thirteen
only the x cubed coefficients matter
the ratio of the leading coefficients is eleven over thirteen

steps.why: The other terms go to 0, so the value is the ratio of the coefficients of x³.
common_mistakes: Trying to reduce 11/13 further; 11 and 13 have no common factor.
steps.memory_tip: Only the x³ coefficients matter: 11 over 13.

insider_note: Divide every term by the HIGHEST power present, x³, and each remaining fraction goes to 0. The answer is just the ratio of the leading coefficients, 11/13.
